opening_message: There's a shrub or small tree along the edge of my yard that's gotten pretty big. Does anyone know what kind of plant this actually is?

slots.name: leaf_size_shape
slots.value: The leaves are pretty big, maybe six or seven inches long, kind of oval-ish, and they're arranged directly across from each other on the stem, not staggered.
slots.description: Large opposite leaves (roughly 4-8 inches) match fringetree, not Chinese privet, whose opposite leaves only run 1-2 inches long.

slots.name: leaf_persistence_season
slots.value: It loses all its leaves in the winter -- right now there's nothing on it at all.
slots.description: Fully deciduous habit matches fringetree; Chinese privet in this region is evergreen or semi-evergreen and keeps most of its leaves through winter.

slots.name: bloom_appearance
slots.value: Back in the spring it had these big, wispy white flower clusters hanging down, almost like white fringe or a cloud, and they smelled pretty nice.
slots.description: Large (4-8in), fragrant, drooping fringe-like white flower panicles match fringetree; Chinese privet's flowers are under an inch long on 2-3in panicles and smell unpleasant ("fetid"), not fragrant.

slots.name: bark_texture
slots.value: The bark's kind of grayish-brown and flaky, breaks off in little thin flakes if you pick at it.
slots.description: Thin, flattened bark broken into small plates matches documented fringetree bark texture, distinct from privet's smoother bark.

slots.name: growth_rate
slots.value: It hasn't really gotten much bigger the past few years, grows pretty slow.
slots.description: Slow growth (roughly 6-10 inches/year) and no aggressive spreading matches fringetree; Chinese privet resprouts vigorously and spreads by root suckers and bird-dispersed seed.

slots.name: nearby_plants
slots.value: There's a fence line right behind it and a couple other bushes nearby that look different from this one.
slots.description: Background color about the surrounding planting -- doesn't change the correct identification or framing for this plant.

slots.name: ownership_duration
slots.value: Only moved in a year or two ago, so not totally sure how long it's been there.
slots.description: How long the homeowner has owned the property -- doesn't change which identification or framing applies here.

ecological_framing_notes: Fringetree is a native ornamental tree valued by songbirds and pollinators for its fruit and fragrant flowers, with no invasive designation or control recommendation from NC State Extension. A correct answer should identify it as fringetree (not Chinese privet), note that no removal is needed, and ideally encourage keeping it rather than merely declining to recommend treatment.
